To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
oxidized lipoprotein (ox-LDL or ox-HDL3) inactivate endothelium derived relaxing factor (NO) in a concentration-dependent manner by reacting with the NO molecule.
the lipid components of lipoproteins, especially oxidized lipoprotein, inactivate EDRFs.

lipoproteins oxidized in vivo or by exposure to Cu2+, inhibit EDRF/endothelium derived relaxing factor-mediated relaxation of vascular smooth muscle cells by inactivating EDRF/EDRF, which is likely to be nitric oxide or a related molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of lipoproteins, especially LDL and its modified forms, in the development of atherosclerosis.
the role of lipoproteins and their oxidized forms in vascular disease, specifically the role of lipids in the inactivation of EDRF.
the mechanisms that underlie the impaired relaxation of blood vessels in hyperlipidemic states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipid component, not protein component, of ox-LDL is responsible for inactivation of NO and that the mechanism of inactivation involves a reaction between the lipid component and NO.
oxidized lipoprotein inactivates EDRF by a direct interaction with EDRF and/or with the target cell.

the inactivation of endothelial cell derived relaxing factors by oxidized lipids is an important mechanism for the impairment of vascular relaxation that is associated with atherosclerosis and hypercholesterolemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxidized lipoprotein impairs the activity of endothelial cell derived relaxing factors (EDRFs) and that this effect is mediated by the lipid component of ox-Lipid.
ox-LDL inhibits the effects of EDF by inactivating it after it is released by endothelial cells.
oxidized lipoprotein inactivation of EDRF/No is mediated by a lipid component of the lipoprotein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxidized lipoprotein is a powerful inhibitor of endothelial cell derived relaxing activity.
oxidized lipoprotein is the major factor in the impairment of endothelial function in atherogenesis.
oxidized lipoprotein inactivate endothelial derived relaxing factors, which is likely to be a major mechanism of vascular dysfunction associated with hyperlipidemia and atherosclerosis.
